recognize_zh: 電子顯微鏡下血管腔內可見多個邊界銳利、長方形或多角形的電子緻密沉積，內部有規則平行條紋（晶格狀，藍箭頭），代表結晶化的單株免疫球蛋白或冷球蛋白，而非無定形的免疫複合體。
features: Multiple sharply demarcated rectangular to polygonal electron-dense deposits
Internal organized substructure with regular parallel striations (crystalline lattice)
Deposits located within a capillary lumen/cell cytoplasm-like space bounded by a basement membrane-like layer
Adjacent cellular elements with mitochondria and a vacuole at the periphery
Variable size of crystals, from small fragments to large blocks
describe_en: Transmission electron micrograph at high magnification shows several sharply marginated, rectangular to polygonal electron-dense deposits within a capillary lumen (blue arrows). The deposits have an organized internal substructure composed of regular parallel linear striations, indicating crystalline organization rather than amorphous immune complexes. Surrounding cellular elements are compressed at the periphery. In a patient with CLL, findings are consistent with intraluminal crystalline deposits of monoclonal immunoglobulin (e.g., crystalline cryoglobulin or crystalglobulin), supporting a paraprotein-related glomerulopathy; immunofluorescence for light-chain restriction is required.

ddx.vs: Ordinary immune complexes are granular without organized substructure, whereas these deposits show a sharp geometric outline with a periodic lattice.

Cryoglobulin deposits typically form curved microtubules or annular structures 20-35 nm in diameter, so tubular versus crystalline substructure plus serum cryoglobulin testing separates them from crystalglobulin.
These crystals are located inside proximal tubular cells or histiocytes, not within capillary lumina.
Fibrillary GN has randomly arranged 10-30 nm fibrils and immunotactoid has parallel 30-50 nm microtubules in the mesangium and GBM, rather than solid lattice crystals in lumens.
